title: The Ohio Public Utilities Commission submits request for approval of Study Agreement re PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.’s 10/13/2026 Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio’s State Agreement Approach Request under ER27-126.

documents.text:
November 3, 2026

         VIA ELECTRONIC FILING

         Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
         Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
         888 First Street, N.E.
         Washington, D.C. 20426

         RE: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER27-126
         Study Agreement in Furtherance of Ohio’s State Agreement Approach Request

         Dear Secretary Reese,

         On October 13, 2026, PJM Interconnection, LLC (PJM) filed with the Federal Energy
         Regulatory Commission (FERC) an executed “Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of
         Ohio’s State Agreement Approach Request” (Study Agreement), designated as FERC Rate
         Schedule No. 54, by and among PJM, SE DC DevCo, LLC, PORTS 2 Interconnect, LLC,
         Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC, and AEP Ohio Transmission Company, Inc. As explained in the
         filing, the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio’s Federal Energy Advocate (Ohio FEA)
         requested, on June 15, 2026, that PJM initiate the State Agreement Approach (SAA) with respect
         to the Flagship Project, an integrated data center, generation, and transmission development
         located at and around the former United States Department of Energy Portsmouth Gaseous
         Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio.

         As explained in the Ohio FEA’s request, designated as Schedule A of the Study Agreement, the
         state of Ohio seeks to utilize the SAA as an efficient method to identify and implement
         transmission solutions needed to serve this critical project in support of Ohio’s public policy
         requirements,1 which are aligned with the federal administration’s objectives for this large-scale
         technology campus.2 Consistent with the SAA, project costs would be assigned to Ohio, and
         would then be further allocated to SB Energy, which has committed to fund the infrastructure
         through arrangements structured to protect other customers.

         The Ohio FEA agrees with PJM that the Study Agreement provides a just and reasonable
         framework that will enable PJM to conduct an integrated and holistic technical evaluation of the

         1
          Ohio Revised Code 4928.02, available at https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4928.02.
         2
          FACT SHEET: The Department of Energy is Ensuring Affordable Energy Access in Ohio While Powering the
         Future of AI, available at https://www.energy.gov/articles/fact-sheet-department-energy-ensuring-affordable-energy-
         access-ohio-while-powering-future.

          proposed load, generation, and transmission, while maintaining PJM’s existing reliability
         requirements and interconnection processes and ensuring that study costs are assessed to the
         project developer. As a key step toward the timely development of the infrastructure necessary to
         support the Flagship Project, the Ohio FEA requests that the Study Agreement be accepted by
         FERC.
